podcast.title: Band Expulsion and Sentencing
podcast.body: Following his arrest, Michael Todd was immediately removed from Coheed and Cambria. At his trial, he received a sentence of one year of home confinement, three years of probation, and a requirement for extensive drug treatment. The leniency in his sentence was partly influenced by his recent diagnosis with testicular cancer. "Todd was immediately kicked out of the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Comic Book and Graphic Novel Creator
podcast.body: Claudio Sanchez, the lead singer and guitarist for Coheed and Cambria, ventured into the world of comic books in 2008 with two issues of "The Bag.OnLine Adventures." He later progressed to graphic novels, most notably the sci-fi series "The Amory Wars," which intricately details the story of the 78 planets of Heaven's Fence and the "key work," the energy beams that bind everything together. "He started in the world of comic books in 2008 with two issues of something called the bag online adventures."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Contemporary Concept Album Artists
podcast.body: Coheed and Cambria is mentioned as one of the contemporary acts currently releasing concept albums. "Hello again, I'm Ellie Cross and with all the concept albums that we're seeing these days, Nine Inch Nails, My Chemical Romance, Coheating Cambria, The Arcade Fire, 30 Seconds to Mars, I thought it might be cool if we went back through the history of Alt Rock to see where all this came from."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Escape and Arrest
podcast.body: After obtaining the drugs, Michael Todd fled the Walgreens, ran across a field behind the building, and jumped into a cab. His intention was to make that night's gig in nearby Mansfield, Massachusetts. However, security cameras at the pharmacy and witness identification of the cab company allowed authorities to track the cab to the Coheed and Cambria tour bus in the venue's parking lot, where Todd was arrested before the band took the stage. "Before the bank had hit the stage that night, Todd was arrested."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Fan Scamming and Financial Troubles
podcast.body: Despite a lenient sentence for the robbery, Michael Todd later admitted to scamming fans of Coheed and Cambria. He accepted money for band merchandise that he did not actually own or possess, further contributing to his financial problems, particularly in light of his ongoing cancer treatments. "But then, he admitted to scamming fans of the band by accepting money to sell co-heat and Cambria merchandise that he didn't actually own."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Taylor Hawkins' Collaboration and Touring
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins performed on an album by Coheed and Cambria and also toured with them for a period. This highlights his willingness to collaborate with and support other bands outside of his main projects. "He performed on a co-heating Cambria album and even toured with them a bit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unexpected Warped Tour Resume Entry
podcast.body: Coheed and Cambria is listed among artists whose participation in the Warped Tour might be unexpected, showcasing the diversity of acts the festival attracted. "Here are some other artists that you may not have expected to have warped on their resume. Coheeding Cambria..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Walgreens Robbery Attempt
podcast.body: In July 2011, while on tour with Soundgarden, Coheed and Cambria's bass player Michael Todd was arrested for attempting to rob a Walgreens drug store in Massachusetts. He entered the store and showed the pharmacist a note on his Blackberry stating, "I have a bomb, give me some oxycontin or else." When no OxyContin was available, he demanded 30-milligram Percocets plus Oxycodone. "He was arrested for trying to rob a Walgreens drug store in Massachusetts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Arrest and Departure from Coheed and Cambria (July-August 2011)
xref.body: After the Walgreens robbery, Michael Todd was tracked down via the taxi company and arrested on charges of possession and armed robbery, held on $10,000 bail. The band's keyboard player filled in on bass for that night's show, and Todd officially left the band on August 4, 2011. "Todd left the band on August 4."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: OxyContin Addiction and Armed Robbery (July 10, 2011)
xref.body: As the bassist for Coheed and Cambria, Michael Todd developed an addiction to OxyContin. On July 10, 2011, during a tour stop in Mansfield, Massachusetts, he took a taxi to a Walgreens in Adelboro, where he robbed the pharmacist of six bottles of OxyContin by threatening them with a bomb via a message on his phone. "He got hooked on OxyContin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Guest Appearances and Collaborations
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins was known for his willingness to assist other bands and artists. He performed on albums by Coheed and Cambria (also touring with them), Eric Avery (Jane's Addiction bassist), Chris Shiflett (Foo Fighter, for Jackson United project), Slash, Ozzy Osborne, and Elton John. "And like his boss and friend, Taylor was always willing to help out other bands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
